correctness.rationale: For vertices in one part, closed neighborhoods differ only by the vertex itself, while vertices from different parts have closed-neighborhood union equal to the whole graph. This reduces the two liar-domination inequalities exactly to the capacity bound stated in the claim. The generating function follows from independent binomial choices inside parts; the minimum-size condition is exactly bounded-profile feasibility. The packaged verifier checks the literal definition, the criterion, all coefficients, and the minimum through order 9 without mismatch.

value.rationale: The result upgrades an established fault-tolerant domination invariant from known scalar special-family evaluations to a complete feasible-set description on arbitrary complete multipartite graphs. The exact enumerator and minimum-set count are natural data for reliability, random placement, and extremal questions, while the capacity criterion exposes the structural reason the dense host family simplifies.
